question: A patient on diazepam 10 mg daily for 6 months, who now wants to stop, should be advised to discontinue the drug abruptly over 2–3 days to minimise the duration of withdrawal discomfort.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. Unlike opioid withdrawal (unpleasant but rarely fatal), benzodiazepine withdrawal seizures can be fatal. Chronic benzodiazepine use must always be tapered gradually. A 10–25% dose reduction per week is the minimum safe approach; individual tolerance varies.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Abrupt discontinuation of benzodiazepines after chronic use risks life-threatening withdrawal seizures. The correct approach is a slow taper — typically reducing the dose by 10–25% per week (or slower if withdrawal symptoms emerge), often substituting a long-acting benzodiazepine such as diazepam to smoothen the reduction. Abrupt cessation is contraindicated.
